 Your 2026 Michigan general election voter guide
 Election Day is on Tuesday, Nov. 3
 Samantha Sayles , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  October 26, 2026 at 5:00 AM Updated:  October 26, 2026 at 5:18 AM Tags:  Decision 2026 , Michigan , Elections A close-up view of "I Voted" stickers at Maples Elementary School on primary election day, Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026, in Dearborn, Mich. (AP Photo/Nic Antaya) CORRECTION: Corrects location to Dearborn NOT Detroit (Nic Antaya, Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.) Michigan voters will decide key races and two statewide proposals in the November general election.
 Here’s what voters need to know: 
 Recommended Videos
 When is Election Day, and what time do polls open and close?
 Election Day is on Tuesday, Nov. 3. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. 
 All qualified voters in line at 8 p.m. will be allowed to vote.
 What are the major races in the 2026 general election?
 Major races in the 2026 Michigan General Election include governor, secretary of state, attorney general, the Michigan Supreme Court, and more.
 What proposals will appear on the ballot?
 Two proposals will appear on the ballot statewide for Michigan voters. Proposal 1 asks voters to decide whether to rewrite Michigan’s Constitution. Proposal 2 asks voters to decide whether to restrict funding for political campaigns.
 Read more --> Here are the proposals on Michigan’s November 2026 ballot 
 How do I check if I’m registered to vote?
 To check your voter registration status, visit the Michigan Voter Information Center . There, you can search for your voter information by name or driver’s license number.
 Read more --> Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here’s how to check 
 How can I track election results?
 You can track election results here on Election Day. 
 Watch Local 4+ at 8 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3, to watch for live updates on the latest election results.
 Related --> Why aren’t Michigan election results instant? How our votes are counted 
 What’s on my ballot?
 To see your sample ballot for the 2026 November general election, visit the Michigan Voter Information Center .
 Related --> What happens to your ballot after you vote in Michigan? 
 Where do I go to vote?
 To find your polling location, visit the Michigan Voter Information Center . You can also find information about your registration status, track your absentee ballot and more.
 Can I vote a “split” ticket in the November general election?
 Yes. Voters can “split” their ticket in the November general election. Michigan voters can also vote straight-ticket by selecting the option on the side of their ballot with partisan races. Voting straight ticket does not automatically include selections on the non-partisan side of the ballot.
 Do I need to vote the entire ballot?
 Michigan voters do not have to vote on the entire ballot. You can choose the races or ballot questions you want to vote on. Skipping sections on the ballot does not invalidate your ballot.
 Can I still register to vote on Election Day?
 Eligible voters can register to vote up to and on Election Day. 
 Voters can register or update their voter registration in person at their local clerk’s office through 8 p.m. on Election Day.
 What do I need to register to vote?
 You must provide proof of residency if you are registering within 14 days of an election.
 Proof of residency includes the following:
 Michigan driver’s license, state ID or U.S. Passport 
 A utility bill 
 Insurance documents 
 Bank or credit card statement 
 Financial aid or school enrollment documents 
 A lease agreement 
 A paycheck or other government check 
 Other government document 
 You will be asked for a photo ID when registering to vote in person. If you don’t have one, you can sign a form called an affidavit and then register to vote.
 Applications must be received by, or postmarked as sent to your local clerk’s office at least 15 days before Election Day in order to be processed in time for the next election. Within 14 days of an election, voters must submit a voter registration application in person and present proof of residency at their local clerk’s office.
 Explainer --> Michigan law allows voting without photo ID: What to know 
 Who can register to vote in Michigan?
 Michigan voters must be at least 16 years old, a U.S. citizen, and not currently serving a sentence in jail or prison to preregister or register to vote online, by mail, at a self-service station, or at a Secretary of State office no later than two weeks before Election Day. 
 Eligible citizens can register to vote or update their voter registration up to and on Election Day in person at their local clerk’s office.
 What if I moved since the last election?
 The address on your driver’s license and voter registration has to match. If you updated your driver’s license with your new address, your voter registration has been updated, too. If not, you can do this in person at any SOS branch office or your local clerk’s office. 
 How can I vote for someone whose name is not on the ballot?
 The ballot will include space for you to write in the name of someone who is not listed. 
 Write-in votes will be counted only if that person has filed a declaration of intent to be a write-in candidate.
 Can I wear political clothing or bring campaign items with me to the polls?
 If you wear a button or shirt with election-related images or slogans, you will be asked to remove it. 
 You can carry literature for personal use only, but you can’t distribute it or leave it at a polling place.
 Can I vote if I’m unemployed or have been through foreclosure?
 Yes. Employment and home foreclosure status do not affect your eligibility to vote.
 Are firearms allowed in a polling place?
 No. Possessing a firearm is prohibited within 100 feet of a polling place or early voting site while voting is happening; within 100 feet of an absentee voter drop box or clerk’s office for 40 days before the election; or in other voting-related locations, with limited exceptions, including for law enforcement.
 Can I take photos at the polls?
 Voters can take photos of their own ballot in the voting booth. 
 Voters may not hold up their ballot for a selfie. However, voters can take selfies outside the polling location.
